prompt: What is a cohort, in the lesson's sense?

choices.text: Everybody active this week, whenever they installed
choices.why: That mixes new and old; a cohort does not.

choices.text: The people who pay for the app
choices.why: That is a segment, not a cohort by start date.

choices.text: The installs of one week
choices.why: Right. People who started at the same time.

choices.text: One phone model's users
choices.why: That is a device split.

prompt: Why can the total of active users rise while retention gets worse?

choices.text: New installs outweigh faster departures
choices.why: Right. Only cohorts show each group leaving.

choices.text: Active users are counted twice
choices.why: They are distinct.

choices.text: Retention ignores new users
choices.why: Each new cohort is followed too.

choices.text: It cannot; the two always move together
choices.why: They often move apart.

prompt: In the lesson's table, what share of the cohort of 14 September came back in week 1, in per cent?
Why does the cohort of 28 September have no week 4 in the table?

choices.text: Nobody from it came back in week 4
choices.why: Nobody would print 0%, not a gap.

choices.text: The cohort was too small
choices.why: It has 300, like the others.

choices.text: SQLite limits results to four columns
choices.why: No such limit.

choices.text: That week ends after the data does
choices.why: Right. An unfinished week would look like a fall.

prompt: Why is 9% DAU/MAU not alarming for the planner?

choices.text: Every app has 9%
choices.why: Messaging apps are far higher.

choices.text: People study a few days a week
choices.why: Right. That caps DAU/MAU whatever the app's quality.

choices.text: The month was short
choices.why: MAU is always 30 days.

choices.text: DAU/MAU is meaningless for any app
choices.why: It means a lot for daily apps.

prompt: On 26 October, WAU was 247 and MAU 652. What is WAU/MAU, rounded to a whole per cent?
DAU/MAU rose from 9% to 12% over a month. What might explain it besides people coming more often?

choices.text: Nothing else can raise it
choices.why: A falling MAU raises it too.

choices.text: MAU fell as occasional people left
choices.why: Right. The cohort table tells the two apart.

choices.text: A new phone model that more people use daily
choices.why: Device does not change the ratio by itself.

choices.text: Daylight saving time
choices.why: Not a cause of a month's ratio.

prompt: Why does no event mark the moment somebody uninstalls the planner?

choices.text: The stores delete the event
choices.why: There is no event to delete.

choices.text: Analytics libraries batch it for a month
choices.why: There is nothing to batch.

choices.text: Uninstall events are forbidden by law
choices.why: No law forbids it; it is impossible from the app.

choices.text: The app is not running then
choices.why: Right. Nothing of yours can send it.

prompt: The planner defines churn as 14 days without an app_open. A person returns on day 16. What does the rule report?

choices.text: Churned at 14, back at 16
choices.why: Right. Churn is always an estimate.

choices.text: A new install
choices.why: Same install id; it is a return.

choices.text: Nothing; the rule waits for day 30
choices.why: It fires at 14.

choices.text: An error in the data
choices.why: It is ordinary, and why the rule is an estimate.

prompt: Which of these are signs of churn the planner can actually see? Choose every one.

choices.text: Days with no app_open from an install
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Notifications switched off, read at the next launch
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A push that can no longer be delivered
choices.why: Right. Often the first sign of an uninstall.

choices.text: An uninstall event sent by the iOS app
choices.why: The app is gone; it sends nothing.

prompt: Which change does the lesson say moves retention the wrong way?

choices.text: Suggesting a first session on the first visit
choices.why: That helps week 1.

choices.text: A smaller app
choices.why: That helps people keep it.

choices.text: Notifications nobody asked for, sent to bring people back
choices.why: Right. They teach people to switch notifications off.

choices.text: A reminder the person chose
choices.why: That reminds them of their own plan.

prompt: A new onboarding screen ships to everybody on 1 October. Why is comparing September and October cohorts a weaker test than releasing it to half the new installs?

choices.text: Other changes get mixed in
choices.why: Right. Anything else that changed between the months is mixed in; half and half, in the same weeks, isolates the change.

choices.text: Retention cannot be measured in October
choices.why: It can.

choices.text: October cohorts are always smaller
choices.why: Size is not the weakness.

choices.text: Feature flags make the app faster
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

prompt: Lesson 16's funnel lost the most people between adding a course and planning a ___.
Order the planner's activity counts on 26 October from smallest to largest.
Match each kind of app to the churn window that fits it.
Which number in the lesson is the most important for the planner's first week?

choices.text: MAU
choices.why: A month mixes every cohort.

choices.text: Installs in the first week
choices.why: They say nothing about coming back.

choices.text: Week-1 retention of each cohort
choices.why: Right. Six in ten leave there.

choices.text: DAU/MAU
choices.why: Capped by the habit, not the first week.
